capabilities.target: any customer account record, by email or account id

instructions.note: The agent may look up any customer 'by email or account id', with the account identifier taken from the untrusted ticket content rather than restricted to the authenticated requester's own record.

The only stated control against cross-customer disclosure is a prompt instruction ('Never share another customer's information'). There is no structural check that the customer looked up matches the person emailing.

Escalation to a human is conditioned solely on the model's own judgment of whether 'the customer is angry', which is a subjective, model-determined trigger rather than a structural gate, and does not cover calm-toned malicious requests.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model following an in-prompt instruction against a competing goal injected via the untrusted email. A more capable model can be talked into exceptions ('the customer clearly needs this information to resolve their own issue') more competently.

controls.name: Escalate to a human only if the customer appears angry
controls.decay_rationale: The decision to involve a human is made entirely by the model's own sentiment judgment; it is not a structural gate and does not trigger for calm-toned malicious requests. It provides no protection for the cross-customer disclosure scenario.

controls.name: Outbound email logging to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Logging is enforced outside model control, but it is detective only and does not prevent the send; it only helps if someone reviews the logs.

controls.name: Recipient bound to the ticket's verified originating address
controls.decay_rationale: Would not depend on model behavior since the destination would be pulled from the system of record rather than chosen by the model or email body content.

controls.name: CRM lookup scoped to the authenticated requester's own record
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcing scope at the credential or query layer would sever the cross-customer lookup path regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval before cross-account or first-time-recipient sends
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate does not decay with model capability, unlike the current instruction-only escalation heuristic.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta with confused-deputy credentials (TC1 + TC4): untrusted email drives cross-customer CRM read and autonomous email send

attack_path.note: Untrusted customer email content can specify which account or email address to look up (prompt.md:3 permits lookup by email or account id supplied in the request).
get_customer executes with CRM_SVC_TOKEN, a broad credential able to read any customer record, not scoped to the requester's own identity.
mail_mcp.send is invoked autonomously for 'routine' tickets using MAIL_SVC_TOKEN, a shared service account able to send to any address, with no structural approval gate.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: The model is configured through an environment variable and upgraded with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable = true). Watch for that env var / model version changing, and for rising bypass rates against the 'never share' and 'escalate if angry' prompt instructions.

evidence.observation: Agent looks up customer accounts by email or account id supplied in the ticket, with no restriction to the requester's own identity.
Routine tickets are answered and sent directly without human review; escalation depends solely on the model's own judgment of customer anger.
crm_mcp and mail_mcp each authenticate with a single static bearer token shared across all requests, not per-user scoped credentials.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address.
The only control against cross-customer disclosure is a single behavioral prompt instruction.

recommendations.action: Scope CRM access (or add an application-layer check) so a ticket can only retrieve the record of the authenticated requester matched by verified email or account id, not an arbitrary identifier supplied in the message body.
Bind the outbound recipient to the original ticket requester's verified address from the system of record; do not let the model choose or add recipients.

Add a raw-action human approval gate before any send that includes data from a customer record different from the requester, or before any first-time send to a new recipient. Replace the sentiment-based escalation heuristic with this structural gate.
Alert in the SIEM when an outbound email's recipient does not match the ticket's originating address, and review these alerts on a defined cadence.

rating.rationale: An untrusted customer email can direct a lookup of any customer's confidential record via a broadly scoped CRM credential, and the agent autonomously sends the resulting content externally through a shared mail service account able to reach any address (U source to S3 sink, inherent = critical, per rubric section 4). The only preventive controls are two behavioral, capability-dependent prompt instructions (the 'never share' rule and the anger-based escalation heuristic); per rubric section 5 step 4 these earn a single capped -1 tier credit, giving a residual of high. No structural credential scoping, recipient binding, or real approval gate exists, so no step 1, 2, or 3 credit applies. The model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, so the model_upgrade trigger directly threatens both behavioral controls; removing their credit returns the finding to critical, which sets the forecast tier.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes provided, not the observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No IaC or full runtime configuration was supplied; autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not specified in the artifacts and are treated as null/unbounded, which is the conservative reading under the rubric.
Credential scope claims for CRM_SVC_TOKEN and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN are taken as declared from the runtime notes and have not been independently verified against IAM policy or MCP server configuration.
Only one input source (inbound customer email) and two capabilities were provided; any additional tools, memory stores, logging destinations, or peer agents are out of scope for this assessment.
